section: Ashoka - accession, Kalinga War, Dhamma and its content, Dhamma Mahamatras
subsections: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: The Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya, which replaced the viharayatra, was undertaken by Ashoka in which regnal year?
accepted.x: Ashoka undertook the Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya in the 11th regnal year, replacing the earlier practice of viharayatra. This is mentioned in Rock Edict VIII.
accepted.tq: Use the direct year-edict association to distinguish the major stages of Ashoka’s reign.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya — Rock Edict III
Quinquennial tours of rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas — Rock Edict V
Independent judicial authority to rajukas — Rock Edict VI
accepted.x: The appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras is recorded in Rock Edict V. The Dhammayatra is associated with Rock Edict VIII, the quinquennial tours with Rock Edict III, and judicial authority to rajukas with Pillar Edict IV.
accepted.tq: Check the official-edict pairing first and eliminate swapped edict numbers.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka’s administrative measures:
1. Quinquennial tours were undertaken by rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas.
2. These tours were instituted in the 12th regnal year.
3. The quinquennial tours are mentioned in Rock Edict III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Ashoka prescribed quinquennial tours by rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas in the 12th regnal year, as recorded in Rock Edict III.
accepted.tq: Combine the officer group, regnal year and edict number before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed in which of the following years and under which edict?
accepted.x: Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed in the 14th regnal year, as stated in Rock Edict V. The reference to the 13th year represents thirteen years after consecration and should not be confused with the regnal-year entry in the table.
accepted.tq: Separate the regnal-year figure from the phrase ‘years after consecration’ in a close-number trap.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: The reference to the appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras in the ‘13th year’ is best understood as:
o: the 13th regnal year after Ashoka’s accession
the 13th year after the Third Buddhist Council
the 13th year after the Kalinga War
accepted.x: The expression ‘13th year’ in this context means 13 years after consecration. The regnal-year table identifies the appointment as occurring in the 14th regnal year.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a regnal year and a duration calculated from consecration.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s:
With reference to Dhamma Mahamatras, consider the following statements:
1. They worked among all sects.
2. They worked among women and prisoners.
3. Their activities extended to frontier peoples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dhamma Mahamatras worked among all sects, women, prisoners and frontier peoples. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Test the full range of beneficiaries rather than stopping at the first two familiar groups.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Rajukas were given independent judicial authority by Ashoka in the:
o: 26th regnal year through Pillar Edict IV
11th regnal year through Rock Edict VIII
14th regnal year through Rock Edict V
12th regnal year through Rock Edict III
accepted.x: Ashoka granted independent judicial authority to the rajukas in the 26th regnal year. This measure is recorded in Pillar Edict IV.
accepted.tq: Link the administrative power with both its late regnal year and the correct pillar edict.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Who among the following could report to Ashoka at any time?
accepted.x: Pativedakas, or reporters, were permitted to report to the king at any time. This provision is associated with Rock Edict VI.
accepted.tq: Use the functional meaning of the official’s title to identify the correct office.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashokavadana — Pali account centred on Nigrodha
accepted.x: Ashokavadana is a Sanskrit Buddhist legend associated with Upagupta, Taxila and the transformation of Chandashoka into Dharmashoka. Nigrodha belongs to the Sri Lankan Pali tradition represented by the Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped language, source tradition and associated figure in the incorrectly matched pair.

accepted.s: In the Ashokavadana tradition, who is portrayed as Ashoka’s guide?
accepted.x: Upagupta is portrayed as Ashoka’s guide in the Ashokavadana or Divyavadana tradition. Nigrodha and Mahinda are associated with the Sri Lankan Pali accounts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the named religious figures by matching each one with its literary tradition.

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets is associated with the Ashokavadana or Divyavadana tradition?
o: Upagupta, Taxila campaign and the transformation of Chandashoka into Dharmashoka
Nigrodha, 99 brothers and the mission of Mahinda
Mahadeva, Mahishamandala and the Third Buddhist Council
Antiochus II, Magas and Antigonus Gonatas
accepted.x: The Ashokavadana or Divyavadana, written in Sanskrit, associates Ashoka with Upagupta, the Taxila campaign and the legend of Chandashoka becoming Dharmashoka.
accepted.tq: Identify the literary tradition through its distinctive cluster of associated names and episodes.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa:
1. They belong to the Sri Lankan Pali tradition.
2. Nigrodha is associated with these accounts.
3. They refer to the mission of Mahinda.
4. The Mahavamsa portrays the early Ashoka as cruel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa are Sri Lankan Pali accounts associated with Nigrodha and Mahinda, and the Mahavamsa depicts early Ashoka as cruel.
accepted.tq: Check whether all details belong to the same regional and linguistic tradition before choosing the inclusive option.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the Ashokavadana and the Mahavamsa traditions?
o: Ashokavadana is a Sri Lankan Pali chronicle, whereas Mahavamsa is a Sanskrit account associated with Taxila.
Ashokavadana is a Sanskrit tradition associated with Upagupta, whereas Mahavamsa is a Sri Lankan Pali tradition associated with Nigrodha and Mahinda.
Both are Sanskrit works centred exclusively on Mahinda’s mission.
Both traditions reject the transformation of Ashoka from Chandashoka to Dharmashoka.
accepted.x: Ashokavadana or Divyavadana is a Sanskrit tradition associated with Upagupta and the Chandashoka-Dharmashoka legend. Mahavamsa is a Sri Lankan Pali tradition associated with Nigrodha and Mahinda.
accepted.tq: Compare the two traditions across language, region and principal figures rather than by a single name.

accepted.s: Who is associated with the enlargement of the Amaravati stupa by Ashoka?
accepted.x: Ashoka enlarged the Amaravati stupa that had been built by Mahadeva. A plaque bearing Ashoka’s name is associated with this tradition.
accepted.tq: Use the builder–enlarger distinction to avoid confusing Mahadeva with Ashoka.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka and Andhra:
1. Ashoka enlarged the Amaravati stupa built by Mahadeva.
2. A plaque bearing Ashoka’s name is associated with the Amaravati stupa.
3. Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras.
4. Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri edicts are located in the Kurnool-Nandyal region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Andhra-related evidence includes the Amaravati stupa tradition, the plaque bearing Ashoka’s name, the mention of Andhras in Rock Edict XIII, and the Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri edicts in the Kurnool-Nandyal region.
accepted.tq: Combine monument, inscription and location clues to test the complete Andhra connection.

accepted.s: Mahadeva, mentioned in connection with the Amaravati stupa, went to which region after the Third Buddhist Council?
accepted.x: Mahadeva went to Mahishamandala after the Third Buddhist Council. He is also associated with the construction of the Amaravati stupa enlarged by Ashoka.
accepted.tq: Match the missionary figure with the destination rather than with the monument alone.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events or associations in chronological order according to the regnal years given:
A. Rajukas receive independent judicial authority
B. Dhammayatra to Bodh Gaya
C. Dhamma Mahamatras are appointed
D. Quinquennial tours by rajukas, pradeshikas and yuktas
accepted.x: The correct order is Dhammayatra in the 11th year, quinquennial tours in the 12th year, appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras in the 14th year, and judicial authority to rajukas in the 26th year.
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest regnal years first, then resolve the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Dhamma officials and tours - regnal year

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the Hellenistic contemporaries named in Rock Edict XIII?
accepted.x: Rock Edict XIII names Antiochus II, Ptolemy II, Magas, Antigonus Gonatas and Alexander of Epirus. Seleucus I is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Compare each option against the named contemporary list and identify the outside entry.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Hellenistic contemporary)
a. Antiochus II
b. Ptolemy II
c. Magas
 d. Alexander of Epirus

List-II (Reference)
i. Named in Rock Edict XIII
 ii. Named in Rock Edict III
 iii. Associated with the Mahavamsa
 iv. Associated with the Ashokavadana
accepted.x: Antiochus II, Ptolemy II, Magas and Alexander of Epirus are all named as Hellenistic contemporaries in Rock Edict XIII. The other references belong to different subjects and traditions.
accepted.tq: Start with the repeated sure pair: every listed Hellenistic ruler belongs to Rock Edict XIII.

accepted.s: Ashoka is regarded as the first Indian king to address his people directly through:
o: Pali chronicles composed in Sri Lanka
royal genealogies written exclusively in Sanskrit
accepted.x: Ashoka is regarded as the first Indian king to address his people directly through inscriptions, which were written in Prakrit. This represents a direct royal communication with the people.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise medium and language rather than selecting a related literary tradition.
